scenarios.title: Change jobs after the turnover
scenarios.objective: Switch from attacking support to defensive recovery when possession changes.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. YOU and F1 were supporting, but D1 has won the puck and F2 is still below the play. Gold now attacks -x toward the left net. The turnover changes the useful relationship immediately.
cues: Gold attacks -x toward the left net.
F2 is below the play and needs a new scan.

questions.prompt: What fact changes YOU's earlier attacking plan?

options.text: YOU is the higher navy skater

questions.explanation: D1 is the new puck owner, so the possession relationship has changed.

questions.prompt: Which two cues shape your new defensive job?

options.text: F2's route toward the left net
The old support lane as if Navy still had possession

questions.explanation: The new carrier and second attacker set the recovery problem; the old attacking plan is stale.

questions.prompt: Put this turnover response in order.

options.text: Find F2 and the left net

questions.explanation: The job changes at the turnover, then the route is chosen from the new threat picture.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward a recovery position between F2 and the left net.
questions.explanation: This point moves back toward the gold attacking side while keeping F2 visible.

questions.prompt: D1 loses the puck back to F1 before F2 receives. What changes first?

options.text: Re-check possession and return to an attacking support read
Assume F2 still controls the puck

questions.explanation: The second turnover reverses the role cue again. Confirm the carrier before choosing support or pressure.

questions.prompt: How can one skater have two jobs within a few seconds?
questions.explanation: A turnover changes the puck carrier and direction. Explain how the same visible teammates require attacking support before the turnover and defensive recovery after it.

scenarios.title: Close the outlet while forechecking
scenarios.objective: Approach the puck carrier while keeping the nearby outlet in the scan.
scenarios.briefing: Gold attacks -x. D1 carries near the right half wall; D2 is a possible outlet near the blue line. YOU forechecks from inside and F2 is lower. The approach should respond if D1 turns away.
cues: D1 carries near the half wall.
D2 is a possible blue-line outlet.
YOU approaches from inside; F2 is lower support.

questions.prompt: Which gold player is the possible outlet near the blue line?
questions.explanation: D2 is the gold player near the blue-line side of the practice area.

questions.prompt: Which lane checks should shape your acceleration at D1?

options.text: That D1 must pass to D2

questions.explanation: The carrier direction and outlet relationship determine the approach. The outlet is a possibility, not a required pass.

questions.prompt: Arrange this forecheck read.

options.text: Approach on a route that keeps both visible

questions.explanation: The approach is chosen from the carrier and outlet, then updated when the carrier turns.

questions.prompt: Move YOU between D1's half-wall route and D2's outlet.
questions.explanation: This point approaches D1 while retaining a view of D2; it does not promise an interception.

questions.prompt: D1 turns away from D2 and carries down the wall. What should YOU do with the original approach?

options.text: Re-angle toward the new carrier route and re-check D2
Keep the same line as if D1 faced D2

questions.explanation: D1 changed the carrier route, so the original approach is stale. Match the new line while scanning D2.

questions.prompt: How do “half wall” and “blue line” help explain this forecheck?
questions.explanation: They name the carrier area and outlet area so YOU can describe the approach and the space to protect as D1 changes direction.

scenarios.title: Carry until the lane narrows
scenarios.objective: Read the defender and teammate before continuing a two-on-one carry.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. YOU carries toward the right net with F2 across the ice and D1 between the attackers. The still frame supports a choice among carry, pass, or protection after the next cue.
cues: One gold defender is between YOU and F2.
The next choice depends on D1 and the passing lane.

questions.explanation: The setup shows one gold skater, D1; the goalie is separate.

questions.prompt: Which two cues belong in the carry-versus-pass read?

options.text: D1's position relative to YOU's lane
Whether F2 remains a reachable option
Whether the first touch was completed without a new scan

questions.explanation: The defender and teammate lane shape the decision; the picture does not guarantee an outcome.

questions.prompt: Arrange the carrier routine.

options.text: Choose pass, shot or protection after the update

questions.explanation: The carrier uses the available space to gain information, then chooses from the lanes still open.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a continued-carry point that keeps separation from F2 and D1.
questions.explanation: This point advances the carrier while preserving a cross-ice relationship to F2.

questions.prompt: D1 moves into your shooting line and F2 becomes clearly reachable. What deserves a new look?

options.text: A shot through D1 without checking
Keep carrying toward the right net after D1 enters the shooting line

questions.prompt: Name one cue for continuing and one for passing across.
questions.explanation: Continuing fits if the lane and time stay usable; passing fits if D1 commits to YOU and F2 has a reachable open lane. The cues must be re-read.

scenarios.title: Support the loose faceoff puck
scenarios.objective: Offer a second-play option after a faceoff without assuming who won possession.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. The puck is loose at centre ice after the faceoff. YOU is above the dot; both centres are contesting and F2 is wider. The practice rep asks for a support read before committing.
cues: The puck is loose after the faceoff.
Both centres are near the contest.
F2 is a possible second-play option.

questions.prompt: What is the puck state at this freeze?
questions.explanation: The puck has owner null at centre ice, so possession is not established.

questions.prompt: Which two cues should YOU watch?

options.text: Whether F2 can support the new carrier

questions.explanation: Possession and support decide the second play; the label does not tell who will control the puck.

questions.prompt: Arrange the after-faceoff read.
questions.explanation: The support job follows possession and the actual carrier, not a preset faceoff outcome.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into a neutral support space that leaves room for the centre contest.
questions.explanation: This point offers a lane above the contest without crowding either centre.

questions.prompt: Gold C2 gains clean control. What should update first?

options.text: YOU should scan the defensive route toward the left net
Hold the same navy second-play spot

questions.explanation: Gold possession changes the direction and job; re-read C2, F2, and the left-net route.

questions.prompt: How should uncertain possession change your support call?
questions.explanation: Wait for the centre who controls the puck, then support that carrier or recover against the other team. The faceoff freeze does not choose the job.

scenarios.title: Stay above the corner retrieval
scenarios.objective: Support a corner retrieval from the slot side while leaving the carrier room.
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks +x. F2 retrieves a loose puck near the right corner; YOU is above the play and D1 closes the corner. The useful support angle is slot-side, with the net and carrier visible.
cues: F2 is the corner-side navy player.
D1 closes from the corner side.

questions.prompt: Why does YOU have a different first job from F2?

options.text: F2 is closer to the loose puck

questions.explanation: F2 is the nearer navy player to the loose puck; YOU can support from above.

questions.prompt: Which two checks support a slot-side position?

options.text: Whether F2 can see a route out
Whether D1 follows F2 or leaves space
Being closest to the puck at all times

questions.explanation: The carrier's view and defender response make slot support useful; duplicating the corner route can crowd F2.

questions.prompt: Arrange this corner-support response.

options.text: Read F2, D1 and the net
Re-check the exit after F2 controls

questions.explanation: The support route leaves the carrier space and then updates as the exit changes.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a slot-side support point above F2.
questions.explanation: This point supports above the corner and leaves F2 a route out while D1 remains visible.

questions.prompt: D1 wins the puck and carries out of the corner. What changes for YOU?

options.text: Switch from support to a defensive relationship with D1 or the next runner
Stay slot-side as if F2 still controls

questions.explanation: D1 winning possession changes the carrier and direction; re-scan the next gold route.

questions.prompt: How can YOU help a corner retrieval without being closest?
questions.explanation: A slot-side angle gives F2 a visible outlet and can receive a pass while leaving the corner carrier room. It remains conditional on D1's coverage.

findings.issue: The nearest-player key contradicts the supplied coordinates, even though the coach separately assigns F2 as retriever.
findings.evidence: Puck is at (23,-9); YOU at (21,-5) is about 4.5 m away, while F2 at (19,-9) is 4 m away. q1 says F2 is closer without reconciling the explicit retriever assignment.
findings.recommendedChange: Exact question patch: replace option a text with "The coach assigned F2 as the retriever" and replace explanation with "F2 has a different first job because the coach assigned that retrieval; YOU supports from above even though the frozen distances are close." Retain answer ["a"].

findings.issue: One distractor in each affected question is cartoonishly impossible or unsafe instead of a credible U11 misconception, reducing the quality of the decision contrast.
findings.evidence: The affected distractors are: exp26-u11-003-q8 “Pass to yourself through D1”; exp26b-u11-001-q5 “Stop reading and skate into D1”; exp26b-u11-004-q5 “Skate directly into F2’s path”; exp26b-u11-006-q5 “Skate through D1 to the net”; exp26b-u11-007-q5 “Whether D1 has become a teammate”; exp26b-u11-021-q5 “A pass behind the net to no one.”
findings.recommendedChange: Exact option patches: exp26-u11-003-q8 option c -> "Keep offering the same lane without changing your angle"; exp26b-u11-001-q5 option c -> "Carry into the middle without checking whether D1 has closed it"; exp26b-u11-004-q5 option c -> "Stay on the old return line without checking F2’s route"; exp26b-u11-006-q5 option c -> "Keep chasing the rebound as if D1 had not reached it"; exp26b-u11-007-q5 option c -> "Keep the same carry without rechecking F2"; exp26b-u11-021-q5 option c -> "Hold the puck without checking whether F2 becomes reachable".
